gloss: to skip; to leave out; to overtake

definitions.gloss: to skip; to leave out; to omit
definitions.explanation: To pass over something that should have been included — a line while reading, a step in a procedure, or a meal.

definitions.gloss: to overtake; to pass ahead of
definitions.explanation: To get in front of someone who was ahead. Very often used in the passive when someone cuts in line or passes you unfairly.

examples.japanese: {一行|いちぎょう}{抜|ぬ}かして{読|よ}んでしまった。
examples.english: I ended up skipping a line as I read.

examples.japanese: {朝食|ちょうしょく}を{抜|ぬ}かすと{午前中|ごぜんちゅう}に{力|ちから}が{出|で}ない。
examples.english: If I skip breakfast, I have no energy in the morning.

examples.japanese: {手順|てじゅん}を{一|ひと}つ{抜|ぬ}かしただけで、{機械|きかい}が{動|うご}かなくなってしまった。
examples.english: Just leaving out one step in the procedure made the machine stop working.

examples.japanese: {順番|じゅんばん}を{抜|ぬ}かされた。
examples.english: Someone cut in front of me in line.

examples.japanese: {最後|さいご}の{直線|ちょくせん}で{二人|ふたり}{抜|ぬ}かした。
examples.english: I passed two runners on the final straight.

examples.japanese: {列|れつ}に{並|なら}んでいたのに{横|よこ}から{抜|ぬ}かされて、さすがに{腹|はら}が{立|た}った。
examples.english: I was waiting in line and someone cut in from the side, which honestly made me angry.

notes:
TRANSITIVITY: {抜|ぬ}かす is transitive and takes を. Its intransitive partner is {抜|ぬ}ける (to come out, to be missing): {名前|なまえ}が{抜|ぬ}けている (the name is missing) vs {名前|なまえ}を{抜|ぬ}かす (to leave the name out).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {食事|しょくじ}を{抜|ぬ}かす: to skip a meal
- {順番|じゅんばん}を{抜|ぬ}かす: to cut in line
- {腰|こし}を{抜|ぬ}かす: to be so startled one's legs give way (idiom)

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {抜|ぬ}く: to pull out; to overtake — the base verb, more common for passing in a race
- {追|お}い{抜|ぬ}く: to overtake — neutral and specific about passing someone ahead
- {省|はぶ}く: to omit — deliberate and often sensible, whereas {抜|ぬ}かす is usually careless
